title: Customize Commerce in Customer Modules
readerIntent: Learn how customer projects customize commerce without forking framework modules or duplicating state.
priorKnowledge: Read the commerce overview and the capability page you want to extend.
owner: Commerce framework and customer extension owners
summary: Customer modules customize commerce through layered schemas, services, policies, adapters, workflows, pipelines, imports, Axis metadata, tests, and documentation while preserving framework ownership.

sections.heading: Customization principle
paragraphs: The framework should provide reusable capability foundations. Customer projects should extend them in customer modules. Framework modules should not be edited for customer-specific payment providers, delivery partners, attributes, validations, UI labels, reports, or operations.
A customization is healthy when the owning module still owns the state, the customer module adds only the required extension, and Axis remains backend-driven.

sections.heading: What can be customized
items: Schema properties, nested inline objects, referenced child models, indexes, validation, and import/export data.
Service implementations, adapter implementations, provider policy, calculation policy, eligibility policy, and lifecycle actions.
Pipeline steps for single operations such as save, price resolution, checkout placement, reservation, authorization, or publish.
Workflow definitions for long-running business processes such as approval, fulfillment, refund, return, exception handling, and third-party handoff.
BackOffice and Axis metadata: navigation, page heading, help, documentation links, list columns, forms, detail fields, actions, and renderer mappings.
Documentation pages and evidence records for project-specific behavior.

sections.heading: What should not be customized by duplication
items: Do not create a second Product table for UI convenience.
Do not store stock quantity in Product or Cart when Inventory is the authority.
Do not put provider credentials or protocol logic into Axis or CMS content.
Do not hard-code project-specific payment or delivery behavior in generic checkout.
Do not fork framework services when a provider adapter, policy service, or later-layer override can solve the requirement.
Do not add frontend-only rules that are not enforced by backend policy.

sections.heading: Step-by-step extension process
items: Identify the owning capability: Product, Pricing, Inventory, Cart, Order, Payment, Fulfillment, Store, Storefront, CMS, Units, Workflow, Pipeline, or another module.
Decide whether the requirement is data, validation, calculation, provider integration, workflow, UI presentation, documentation, or operations.
Add a customer module with the right dependency order so it layers after the framework module.
Add only the schema fields, services, policies, adapters, or metadata required by the requirement.
Add tests for positive behavior, denial, cross-tenant isolation, permission filtering, failure, retry, idempotency, and backward compatibility.
Expose the result in Axis through backend-driven content and reusable renderers instead of page-specific frontend duplication.
Document what the extension changes, how to configure it, how to operate it, and how to roll it back.

sections.heading: Pipeline and workflow usage
paragraphs: Use a pipeline when one operation needs many deterministic steps. Example: checkout placement validates cart, recalculates totals, confirms stock, authorizes payment, creates order, writes evidence, and returns a result.

Use a workflow when a business process spans multiple tasks, systems, users, or time. Example: fraud review, warehouse pick-pack-ship, refund approval, provider reconciliation, or document delivery to a third-party application.
items: Pipeline steps should be small, testable, idempotent where needed, and owned by the module that performs the operation.
Workflow steps should carry business state, approval state, retry state, and evidence across departments or systems.
Customer modules can add or replace steps through configuration and services, but must preserve the contract of the owning operation.

sections.heading: Axis customization
items: Axis should render lists, tables, detail panels, previews, query builders, forms, help icons, documentation links, and lifecycle actions through reusable components.
Backend content and component models decide which page, component, renderer, fields, columns, and actions apply.
If a customer adds schema fields, Axis should be able to display them through schema-driven metadata or configurable grid/detail definitions.
If a customer adds a provider action, Axis should display it only when backend metadata exposes the action and the logged-in user has permission.
